scope: Current JKRD V5 DAG, queues 1/2/5, and explicitly versioned storage contracts. No executor, no new EX operations.

notation.fields: Every listed field is required unless its name ends with ?. Unknown fields rejected in every typed object. JSON object extension points require an exact registered contract schema.
notation.Bit: JSON numeric 0 or 1; bool is not bit
notation.Integer: JSON safe nonnegative integer, decimal lexical form, no exponent/negative zero/fraction
notation.Index: Integer in the referenced local array range
notation.string: Unicode scalar sequence, no lone surrogate
notation.JSON: standard JSON values subject to the lexical restrictions; this type alone never grants an executable extension

Document.runtime?: Runtime; required for runtime format, forbidden for structure format

Port.id: XId or YId according to containing array

Structure.nodes: Node[] sorted by numeric id; gaps allowed

Capacity.max_live_nodes: PositiveDecimal or null; null means no model-imposed bound, not infinite physical memory

Contract.definition: JSON object governed by exactly this registered contract; embedded declarative templates, operations and parameter schemas, no executable source

BehaviorBinding.arguments: JSON object fully checked by the registered operation parameter schema

StorageDefinition.bootstrap: JSON object governed by contract or null; structure format requires a valid fresh-start bootstrap, runtime may have null

Runtime.arrivals: Arrival[] sorted by target numeric id

Task.bound_ex: BoundEX[] in actual relative auxiliary evaluation order; registered operation places each step at its declared phase among structural/new-node actions, not necessarily immediately after primary EX
Task.cause: Cause[]; audit-only, never live parameter references
Task.protected_reads: Target[] sorted by numeric id; exact union of already-bound ordinary live Q-source dependencies from primary/auxiliary EX; omit locked sources and each EX target own accumulator

Parameters.bits: Bit[]; task-owned flat immutable value pool
Parameters.sources: ParameterSource[] in X-then-Q numeric source order

FrameParameters.indices: Index[]; exactly W=1..8, in bit order, into this same owned Parameters.bits
FrameParameters.channels: (XSource or QSource)[] in the same bit order

BoundEX.condition: registered condition-group name; evaluate once at this task plan entry using current head/result/q, then keep that decision for all group steps; never persist an old Boolean

TaskContext.operation: registered contextual operation name; does not invoke behavior; only behavior_id with the actual primary Q may invoke it
TaskContext.frame: FrameRef or null; historical identity does not bind ACK to arrival-time head

Cause.identity: string; historical input/task/event identity; not dereferenced on restore

Arrival.values: ArrivedValue[] sorted by effective event source numeric id; nonempty strict subset of required sources

Allocators.next_node: Decimal; greater than every physical Q id ever allocated; no id reuse in draft-1

FrameRef.sequence: PositiveDecimal; never reused within that module

StagedInput.value: Bit; not yet accepted into a FRAME_IN frame

Handoff.parameters: Parameters; owner of complete frame while copies remain
Handoff.copy_steps: CopyStep[] in original enqueue order; includes actual W data copies and FRAME_IN copy

CopyStep.completed: boolean; execution progress, not a second business q

Area.live_frames: FrameRef[] in business order; precisely V=1 slots; not an execution FIFO

Block.slots: Slot[] in index order; count exactly accepted_count; no slot reuse in same generation

Slot.claim: QRef or null; PRE requires Q, POST null

RetireSet.nodes: QRef[] sorted by numeric id; candidates, not live protection edges

OutputRequest.data: QRef[] in bit order; independent retained/current slot data; no saved bit mirror

OutputBatch.kind: enum(first,replay); execution record checked against locked marker parameter
OutputBatch.pending: PendingOutput[] in position order; exactly remaining positions

Retention.frame: FrameRef or null; historical identity allowed when validity q revoked
Retention.data: QRef[] for fixed independent H in bit order

fixed_profile.DAG.FIFO: not a field in draft-1; reject even if empty; future enabled profile requires another revision
fixed_profile.rings: reject non-self cycles, SCC suspension, budgets and timers
fixed_profile.failure_state: reject in-flight/uncommitted/failed/suspended/retry state; F03/F04 must define a later profile
fixed_profile.routing: input copy first, then current RAM membership, otherwise Qi; queue name is given by containing FIFO, not duplicated in Task
fixed_profile.contract_rule: Every behavior-affecting module definition is embedded, versioned, hashed and validated against the loader supported contract. A known id without matching definition/schema is insufficient. Unknown extension cannot be ignored.

fingerprint_contract.normalization: Delete only explicit default pro=q=0/1 at structure.nodes[*].pro. All other fields and all array order remain unchanged.

document_payload_fields.format_payload: the full object above, not its digest
document_payload_fields.runtime: document.runtime for runtime format; JSON null for structure format

fingerprint_contract.contract_definition_md5: MD5(UTF8(canonical(Contract.definition))); include Contract definition and this checked digest in structure
fingerprint_contract.meaning: format_md5 identifies current structure, initial values, interfaces and behavioral contracts; md5 additionally identifies format kind and runtime. Neither proves behavior equivalence, provenance or correctness.

canonical_bytes.encoding: UTF-8, no BOM, whitespace or terminal newline
canonical_bytes.arrays: preserve all array order exactly; validate format-required ordering separately
canonical_bytes.strings: no Unicode normalization; escape quote and backslash; U+0008/0009/000A/000C/000D use \b/\t/\n/\f/\r; other U+0000..001F use lowercase \u00xx; other scalar values literal; slash unescaped
canonical_bytes.numbers: nonnegative safe integer in ordinary decimal, no exponent/fraction/negative-zero; large integers stored as canonical decimal strings

semantic_obligations: All live Q, including quiet/pool/retired candidates, obey current JKRD EX, state, source/user count and full DAG constraints; factory lines and causes do not count.
initial_q declares creation values for every live stateful Q exactly once. Runtime.q covers exactly that set with current generation. No stateless saved q.
inputs and outputs are contiguous X/Y ports; Q numbering may have deleted holes after the input-copy prefix. q_y covers each output exactly once with valid default-pro Q.
No separately supplied statistics or inverse reference graph is authoritative: derive counts, effective source classes, routing, users and DAG from saved structure.
Task targets, bound auxiliary targets and live EX sources must exist at matching generations/versions. All identities unique. Task id order is not global scheduler order.

Parameters.bits is immutable and locally owned. sources maps a real source to an index; one binding per source. frames indexes the same bit pool so bit order has one authority. No cross-task payload aliases. Every bit index must be used by source/frame or declared auxiliary contract.

event policy locks exactly effective Qi_J0 sources, including Xi copy values and input-copy publications; ordinary Qi_q sources and target initial accumulator remain live reads at execution. No constant or cause-as-parameter.

frame-handoff policy requires a matching S/C/module behavior, actual W channels, exact frame identity, ordered indices and source-to-frame consistency. Output-latched requires the fixed output contract; do not generalize it to ordinary stateful sources.

An already bound auxiliary EX plan is saved in order with targets, policies, values and contract-defined guards; unresolved operation objects are resolved at execution per contract. No partial execution plan is saved.
Arrivals are the next, strictly incomplete event-source group. Required sources are derived; no default zeros, duplicated sources, ordinary stateful sources or full unqueued group at a safe boundary.

Handoff copies may be partly completed. Every incomplete CopyStep has exactly its matching Xi task and bit; completed steps have no pending copy task. The last copy creates adjacent independent S/C tasks exactly once and releases handoff. Every handoff has an incomplete step at a saved boundary.
FRAME_IN=0 clears only input_staging. Accepted handoffs/tasks/slots are unaffected. No external current Xi value is needed or restored.
Storage members/roles/block slots/rounds/frontier/requests refer to current Q; PRE/POST data and business control are only JK q, not duplicated bits/flags in module metadata.

Block slots 0..accepted_count-1 remain until eligible full-block release; V=0 at partial capacity does not reset accepted_count or generation. Freed capacity has no Q nodes; reuse increments generation.

GC candidate-set internal edges disappear atomically; external task/EX/arrival/bound-plan dependencies still protect. Candidate references alone are not protection edges. Historical cause and old frame identity need not name live slots.
Output requests are business order, not a FIFO. A request becomes active only at BUSY=0 and request head; restored metadata cannot override BUSY q or rewrite earlier preparation sources.

Output batches pending task ids occur once in RAM.FIFO, all remaining positions prefix..W are covered and order agrees with FIFO; sent prefix has no regenerated task. Marker remains pending until all W data complete; completed rows have no pending items.

FRAME_OUT preserves its own locked marker plus the full bound H/validity EX plan and live source protection. In the current A03 contract H reads protected B.q at execution using ordinary event policy, not historical marker payload. Already emitted bit tasks need not survive. An active preparation retains its actual sources until handoff.
ACK tasks have no frozen arrival-time head. Current head and q qualifications are checked at execution. Old batch completion may not restore consumed-frame validity; frame IDs never reused.

Boundaries contain no running EX, partial RAM transaction, undelivered publication or unfinished current send handoff. Waiting copies/arrivals/requests are allowed; do not wait for future missing sources.

Restore validates the entire detached candidate, then installs atomically, initially paused. It does not execute EX, initialize over current q, publish events, refill arrivals or reconstruct FIFO from output progress.
External output history is not replayed. Input/output sequence cursors support coordinated host continuation; they alone do not provide crash-exactly-once external side effects.
V4 runtime cannot be upgraded losslessly by renaming/supplying empty fields; explicit fresh-start structural import is a separate action with a migration report.

A condition group for first-current-unconsumed FRAME_OUT is checked once before its auxiliary plan; H/CACHE_VALID/F/READY execute under that decision. Rechecking after F changes must not skip READY. Context.operation is an audit/association label, never implicit operation dispatch.

protected_reads explicitly saves expected source generation and EX version for every already-bound ordinary live-read dependency. Its set is checked against primary/bound EX and parameter policies; locked output R sources are not live reads, so their later q changes do not alter old tasks. Source references in current EX remain structurally legal even when their data is locked.
deferred: schema final approval and official format publication
approval and consumer support for the complete A03 contract and six dynamic full-checkpoint fixtures; actual restored-versus-uninterrupted execution

allocator_requirements.global_task: next_task > numeric ordinal of every persisted TaskId, including FIFO tasks, Handoff CopyStep task_ids, output pending task_ids and boundary.last_completed_task_id. It is saved allocation high-watermark, not recomputed from live tasks.
allocator_requirements.input_output: next_input = accepted_input_sequence + 1 and next_output = published_output_sequence + 1 in this no-reservation profile. Both use arbitrary-precision decimal arithmetic.
allocator_requirements.node: next_node is the saved historical allocation high-watermark plus one; at least greater than every current or preserved historical Q ordinal. A deleted maximum node does not lower it. Existing nodes may not be renumbered.
allocator_requirements.module: Every registered module contract declares identity grammar and allocator namespace. Each next_* must exceed every matching allocated ordinal represented in current objects, free capacities or retained historical frame/request/batch/round/handoff references. Unknown identity grammar rejects the contract.
allocator_requirements.history_limit: Absent historical objects cannot reconstruct their former highest ordinal. The persisted next_* value is authoritative; restore must never shrink it by scanning current objects. No hash or local static check proves an unrecorded historical claim.
allocator_requirements.generation: For a reused block id, generation = last_generation + 1; free block records and active blocks with the same id cannot coexist. Fresh physical Q ids are monotonically allocated; node generation is still checked on all saved references.

registered_candidate_extensions.compatibility: Separate exact revision; not implicitly accepted by draft-1 consumers.
